correctness.rationale: The asymmetric condition uses a maximum of two directed closed-neighborhood witness counts, not their sum. With omission set U, the two differences are disjoint and each has size 3 for an edge and 4 for a nonedge; |N[u]|=7 throughout. Consequently all omissions through size 3 work, and for size 4 the only obstructions consist of choosing two from each difference of an adjacent pair. I independently enumerated the set-valued predicate for all 8192 subsets, generated the 39×9 adjacent-pair tetrads with multiplicity, tested every five-set, and canonically grouped four- and five-sets under all 78 affine maps. Counts by omissions 0 through 4 were (1,13,78,286,364) with none larger; the 351 generated tetrads were distinct and exactly the bad four-sets. Five-set obstruction multiplicities were 1:273, 2:312, 3:546, 4:156, with no zero. Monotonicity explains why every larger omission set fails as well. The valid four-sets have seven affine orbits of sizes 26,26,39,39,78,78,78; complementation is equivariant and the displayed detector set passes. These checks reproduce the polynomial and the full claimed structural obstruction.
residual_risks: The exact enumeration is for the labeled graph P13 and the specified affine subgroup only; no claim about other orders or identification of the full automorphism group.

value.rationale: P13 is a standard small strongly regular graph, and DET:IC is a preexisting fault model with a distinct separation rule. The full labeled polynomial gives an exact benchmark beyond the minimum and the partition by affine symmetry makes the optimal patterns reusable. The forbidden-four-set uniqueness and full coverage of five-sets identify what forces the optimum, a meaningful finite cutoff rather than an arbitrary tested slice.
residual_risks: The value is an exact finite benchmark and obstruction classification; no wider Paley-order theorem or practical network performance is asserted.
